liebermann.laws: Abt, Wi, Blas, Ordal, Wal, Pax, Hl, Swer, Að, Mirce, IV Atr, Grið, VIII Atr, Wer, III Atr, Wl lad, VI As, III As, In Cn, Iud Dei, Becwæð, Rect, Geþyncðo, Quadr
liebermann.notes: Transcript and excerpts by Francis Tate, c. 1589–1613, mostly from H (Kentish laws, Blas, Ordal, Wal, Pax, Swer, Að, Mirce, charters, Wer, III Atr, Wl lad, VI As, parts of In Cn, Iud Dei III, Gyf feoh, Becwæð, Geþyncðo), from G (IV Atr, Grið, VIII Atr, parts of the Polity), from B (Rect), and III As from a book of Henry Sidney, Lord President of Wales. In the margin he cites a lost manuscript titled 'Quadripartitus' (Blas Forf, III and VI As, Ordal, III Atr, Pax Wal, Swer, Wer, Wl lad, Geþyncðo, Rect) whose readings match no known Quadripartitus codex.

wormald.shelfmark: London, British Library, Cotton MS Julius C.ii
wormald.wormald_origin: Francis Tate wrote the note on f. 52r (formerly ascribed to Lambarde) (p. 225 nn. 245–6). (Liebermann's guide: transcripts by Tate, c. 1589–1613.)
wormald.laws: Transcript of V Atr and Grið (traced to Joscelyn's copy)
wormald.laws_liebermann: Abt, Wi, Blas, Ordal, Wal, Pax, Hl, Swer, Að, Mirce, IV Atr, Grið, VIII Atr, Wer, III Atr, Wl lad, VI As, III As, In Cn, Iud Dei, Becwæð, Rect, Geþyncðo, Quadr
wormald.overview: An early modern volume of transcripts (Liebermann ascribes them to Francis Tate). A note by Tate on f. 52r, once thought to be Lambarde's, traces its copy of V Æthelred and Grið to a manuscript Joscelyn held by November 1580; Wormald takes this to show that Joscelyn seems then to have had Nero A.i(B), and that Lambarde had probably seen it by that date.
wormald.key_quote: is now known to be by Tate not Lambarde (p. 225 n. 246)
wormald.guide_shelfmark: London, British Library, Cotton MS Julius C.ii
verify_notes: Checked p. 225 nn. 245–6. Overview: 'A volume of Francis Tate's transcripts' is the guide's (Liebermann's) description, not Wormald's — now labelled; Joscelyn's possession of Nero A.i(B) softened to Wormald's 'seems'.
